theme: Corporate strategy across a portfolio of businesses
why_it_matters: The cascade as modelled here assumes a single business competing in an arena. A multi-business parent faces a distinct question - why these businesses are worth owning together, and what the centre contributes that they could not buy - which none of the current tests reach.
evidence: Corporate-level choice is a recurring subject in the series; no source in the index has been confirmed for it.

why_it_matters: Acquisitions are where capability gaps are most often assumed away, and the graph currently treats 'buy' as one word in slot:capability_gaps with no test on whether the acquisition logic holds.

theme: Pricing as a strategy choice rather than a finance exercise
why_it_matters: Price appears in the graph only inside test:customer_action_named. There is no treatment of pricing architecture as an expression of the How-to-Win, which is a common practitioner failure.

theme: Shareholder value maximisation versus customer-first capitalism
why_it_matters: A substantial strand of the author's work argues that optimising for shareholder expectations damages strategy. It bears directly on pillar:winning_aspiration - whose win is being defined - and is entirely absent.

theme: Design thinking and possibility-based problem solving
why_it_matters: concept:possibilities and concept:integrative_thinking are thin stubs of a much larger body of method - generative reasoning, causal modelling, prototyping a strategy - that shapes how possibilities get created in the first place.

theme: Two-sided markets, platforms and network effects
why_it_matters: Where-to-Play and How-to-Win behave differently when the customer set is two populations who value each other. concept:customer_roles gestures at this but no test distinguishes a platform strategy from a linear one.

theme: Strategy without a commercial market - public sector, non-profit, associations
why_it_matters: Several tests are phrased in terms of buying at a price. An organisation whose desired action is enrolment, compliance or donation would fail test:customer_action_named for the wrong reason.
note: This is a false-negative risk in the current rubric, not only a missing topic.

why_it_matters: In regulated arenas the regulator is a party whose behaviour the strategy depends on, and the graph has no place to put that beyond a generic misplaced-should check.

theme: Talent and HR as a functional strategy
why_it_matters: concept:functional_strategy is generic. Talent is the function where 'capabilities' claims most often go to die, and it deserves its own test.

theme: Brand as an expression of the promise, not a communications exercise
why_it_matters: concept:pttc covers the promise; nothing covers how brand choices either reinforce or contradict it.

theme: Strategy in a downturn, and strategic resilience
why_it_matters: Cost cutting under pressure is the moment strategies quietly become 'neither low cost nor differentiated'. The graph catches the end state but not the pressure that produces it.

theme: What AI changes about strategy practice
why_it_matters: Recent instalments of the series engage with this directly. It also bears on this repository's own premise - what an agent should and should not do in strategy work.
Boards approve strategies without owning choices. concept:choice_chartering stops at the executive layer.
Usually arrives as an additive priority list, which is exactly the pattern trap:initiative_list describes, but practitioners will not recognise it as the same thing without a named treatment.

theme: Applying the cascade to a career or an individual
why_it_matters: A recurring reader request in the series. Out of scope for an enterprise coaching agent, recorded so the omission is deliberate rather than accidental.
